claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms multiple primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during solidification.
The alloy exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
An isothermal hold 20–30 K below the primary crystallization onset will suppress extensive primary crystallization.
The proposed hold will enhance amorphous retention.
The proposed hold will improve thermal stability.
The treatment can be applied after either rapid or slower cooling.
The hold limits atomic mobility that would otherwise enable nucleation and growth of primary crystalline phases.
The treatment acts on the early formation of critical crystalline nuclei.
Holding slightly below crystallization onset suppresses nucleation while relaxing residual stress.
The altered kinetics favor vitrification over crystalline phase formation.
The sub-onset hold reduces the thermodynamic driving force for primary crystallization.
The treatment minimizes formation of non-eutectic phases during subsequent heating.
Conventional schedules without the hold cause extensive primary crystallization and limited amorphous retention.
Cooling must be sufficiently rapid to suppress initial crystal growth.
Hold temperatures outside the 20–30 K sub-onset window may fail to inhibit crystalline nucleation.
Successful treatment will delay or reduce DSC crystallization peaks and produce a higher amorphous fraction by XRD and TEM.

contradictions.description: Primary non-eutectic phases are said to form during solidification, but the intervention occurs only during subsequent reheating and is nevertheless claimed to suppress or minimize that earlier primary crystallization. The hypothesis does not explain how post-solidification treatment reverses phases already formed.
The hypothesis specifies a single controlled reheating step, whereas the conditions refer to the treatment being continued under subsequent controlled reheating cycles.
